section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what age can a Nevada teen apply for a learner's permit?
options: a:14 and a half,b:15,c:15 and a half,d:16
note: Nevada allows teens to apply for a learner's permit at age 15½ (15 years and 6 months). The learner's permit requires a parent or guardian's consent and allows supervised driving practice under Nevada's GDL program.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the legal BAC limit for a driver age 21 or older in Nevada?
note: Nevada sets the per se DUI limit at 0.08% BAC for drivers 21 and older. Reaching 0.08% BAC alone is sufficient for a DUI conviction regardless of apparent impairment. Commercial drivers face a stricter 0.04% limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Extreme desert heat in Nevada can cause which tire hazard that drivers should be aware of?
options: a:Tires become sticky and slow the vehicle,b:Tires can over-inflate and potentially blow out due to heat expansion,c:Tires deflate rapidly in hot weather,d:Tires provide more traction in extreme heat
note: Nevada's desert heat causes the air inside tires to expand, which increases tire pressure. An already over-inflated tire can blow out suddenly in extreme heat. Check tire pressure when tires are cold, and follow the vehicle manufacturer's recommended PSI — not the maximum printed on the tire sidewall.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving in Las Vegas and see a pedestrian crossing in a marked crosswalk. What must you do?
options: a:Honk to alert the pedestrian and proceed carefully,b:Slow to 15 mph and pass behind the pedestrian,c:Stop and yield the right of way until the pedestrian has fully crossed your lane,d:Yield only if the pedestrian is directly in your path
note: Nevada law requires drivers to stop and yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks. Las Vegas has extremely heavy pedestrian traffic, especially near the Strip and casino areas. You must remain stopped until the pedestrian has fully cleared your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default speed limit in a Nevada urban area when no speed limit sign is posted?
options: a:20 mph,b:25 mph,c:30 mph,d:35 mph
note: Nevada's default speed limit in urban and residential areas is 25 mph when no other limit is posted. In school zones and near playgrounds, the limit is typically 15 mph when children are present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Nevada highway when a dust storm suddenly reduces visibility to near zero. What should you do?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and pull onto the shoulder to wait it out with feet on the brakes,b:Speed up to exit the dust storm quickly,c:Pull completely off the road, turn off your lights, and wait until the storm passes,d:Continue at reduced speed using your high beams
note: In a severe Nevada dust storm (haboob), pull completely off the paved road surface, turn off your headlights (so other drivers don't follow them into a stopped vehicle), put the car in park, and keep your foot off the brake pedal. Wait until the storm passes before continuing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Nevada's zero tolerance law sets the illegal BAC for drivers under 21 at:
options: a:0.00% — any detectable amount,b:0.02%,c:0.04%,d:0.08%
note: Nevada's zero tolerance law sets the underage DUI threshold at 0.02% BAC for drivers under 21. Any amount at or above 0.02% results in license suspension and other penalties. This is lower than the adult limit of 0.08%.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You want to make a right turn at a red light in Nevada. What must you do?
options: a:Proceed without stopping if no traffic is visible,b:Stop completely, yield to pedestrians and cross traffic, then turn if no sign prohibits it,c:Right turns on red are prohibited statewide in Nevada,d:Signal and proceed — right turns on red have the right of way
note: Right turns on red are permitted in Nevada after a complete stop and yielding to all pedestrians and cross traffic. Always check for 'No Turn on Red' signs, which are common near the Las Vegas Strip and at high-pedestrian intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does Nevada's Move Over law require when passing a stopped emergency vehicle on a multi-lane highway?
options: a:Slow to 15 mph regardless of lane position,b:Move one lane away from the stopped vehicle if safely possible, or slow to a safe speed,c:Stop completely on the shoulder,d:Move over only for law enforcement, not for tow trucks
note: Nevada's Move Over law requires drivers to move one lane away from any stopped emergency, law enforcement, or roadside assistance vehicle with active warning lights. If a lane change is not safely possible, slow to a reasonable speed below the posted limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Nevada, it is illegal to use a handheld cell phone while driving. What is the penalty for a first offense?
options: a:A verbal warning with no fine,b:A fine but no points added to your license,c:A fine and demerit points added to your driving record,d:License suspension for 30 days
note: Nevada's distracted driving law prohibits handheld cell phone use while driving. A first offense results in a fine AND demerit points added to your driving record. Hands-free devices are permitted. Repeat offenses carry higher fines and more demerit points.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are driving on a Nevada highway and the road surface appears wet and shiny despite no recent rain. This may indicate:
options: a:The road was recently sealed and is still wet,b:Black ice — a nearly invisible layer of ice on the road surface,c:Fresh paint markings on the road,d:An optical illusion — the road is dry
note: A wet, shiny road surface in cold weather with no recent rain can indicate black ice — a thin, nearly transparent layer of ice that is extremely dangerous. Black ice forms when temperatures drop and moisture freezes on the road. Slow down immediately and avoid sudden steering or braking inputs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a school bus stopped with flashing red lights on a Nevada highway, what must ALL traffic do on an undivided road?
options: a:Traffic behind the bus must stop; traffic in front may proceed,b:All traffic in both directions must stop at least 15 feet from the bus,c:Slow to 15 mph and pass carefully,d:Stop only if children are visibly exiting
note: In Nevada, on an undivided road, all traffic in both directions must stop at least 15 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights and an extended stop arm. Wait until the lights stop and the arm retracts. On a divided highway with a physical median, only traffic behind the bus must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a Nevada freeway with multiple lanes in each direction, which lane should you use for normal travel?
options: a:The far left (fast) lane at all times for maximum speed,b:The right lanes for normal driving; left lanes for passing only,c:The center lane regardless of speed,d:Any lane — Nevada has no lane use rules
note: Nevada law requires slower vehicles to stay in the right lanes. The left lane on multi-lane freeways is designated for passing — not for sustained travel at the speed limit. Move right after completing a pass. This is especially important on Las Vegas freeways where traffic merges frequently.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the minimum following distance recommended in Nevada under normal highway driving conditions?
options: a:1 second,b:2 seconds,c:3 seconds,d:4 seconds
note: Nevada recommends a minimum 3-second following distance under normal conditions. On Nevada's desert highways, consider increasing to 4 seconds — the roads are long and straight, making it tempting to tailgate, but stopping distances at high speeds remain significant.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must use your headlights in Nevada:
options: a:Only between midnight and 5 AM,b:From 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise, and when visibility is reduced,c:Only when driving outside of city limits,d:Only when other drivers have their headlights on
note: Nevada requires headlights from 30 minutes after sunset to 30 minutes before sunrise and whenever weather or smoke reduces visibility. Using headlights also makes your vehicle more visible to others — turn them on whenever there is doubt.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking on a Nevada street, how far may your vehicle be from the curb?
options: a:6 inches,b:12 inches,c:18 inches,d:24 inches
note: Nevada requires parallel-parked vehicles to be within 18 inches of the curb. Parking further out can obstruct traffic flow and create a hazard. Use your mirrors and take your time to position the vehicle properly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Nevada, what is required before passing a vehicle on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Signal for at least 5 seconds before moving into the oncoming lane,b:Ensure there is a broken yellow centerline on your side, adequate distance, and no oncoming traffic,c:Honk to alert the driver ahead that you are passing,d:Pass on the right shoulder if it is paved
note: Before passing on a two-lane Nevada highway, you must confirm: (1) there is a broken yellow center line on your side, (2) you have a clear view of at least 1/3 mile ahead, (3) no oncoming traffic is close, and (4) you have enough speed and distance to complete the pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does it mean when a traffic signal shows a steady yellow light?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection before the light turns red,b:The light is about to turn green — prepare to go,c:The light is about to turn red — slow down and stop if safe to do so,d:Yield to cross traffic and then proceed
note: A steady yellow signal in Nevada means the light is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop before the intersection if it is safe to do so. Only proceed if you are so close to the intersection that stopping would be unsafe. Never speed up to 'beat' a yellow light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do if your vehicle's brakes fail while driving in Nevada?
options: a:Turn off the ignition to slow the engine,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to build pressure, downshift, use the parking brake gently, and look for an escape route,c:Turn the wheel sharply to generate friction,d:Immediately open your door to create wind resistance
note: If your brakes fail, rapidly pump the brake pedal to try to build hydraulic pressure, downshift to use engine braking, gently apply the parking brake, and steer toward an escape route such as an uphill slope or soft shoulder. Never turn off the ignition while moving as it can lock the steering wheel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A solid white line between lanes of traffic traveling in the same direction means:
options: a:Lane changes are prohibited,b:Lane changes are discouraged but permitted if necessary,c:The lane to your right is an exit lane,d:The lane is closing ahead
note: A solid white line between lanes indicates that lane changes are prohibited at that point. This is commonly used near intersections, at highway entrances and exits, and in construction zones. A broken white line means lane changes are permitted when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on a Nevada interstate and a vehicle is merging from an on-ramp, what should through traffic do?
options: a:Maintain speed — merging vehicles must yield,b:Move to the left lane if possible to give the merging vehicle room,c:Slow to 25 mph and let the merging vehicle enter,d:Flash your headlights to warn the merging driver
note: When safe, Nevada drivers should move left to allow merging vehicles space to enter the freeway. While the merging driver is responsible for matching highway speed and finding a gap, courteous drivers facilitate smooth merging. If moving left is not possible, maintaining steady speed helps merging drivers predict your position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit on most Nevada interstates for passenger vehicles?
options: a:65 mph,b:70 mph,c:75 mph,d:80 mph
note: Most Nevada interstate highways have a speed limit of 75 mph for passenger vehicles in rural areas. Some sections near Las Vegas and Reno have lower limits of 65 mph. Always check posted signs — exceeding the limit on Nevada's open desert highways is a common and costly mistake.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You are approaching a four-way stop at the same time as three other drivers. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The largest vehicle always goes first,b:The driver who arrived first goes first; ties are resolved by yielding to the right,c:All drivers must wait for a signal from a police officer,d:The driver going straight always has the right of way
note: At a four-way stop, the first vehicle to arrive goes first. When two or more vehicles arrive simultaneously, yield to the driver on your right. If all vehicles arrive at exactly the same time, the driver going straight has priority over those turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In Nevada, can you use your horn whenever you feel like it?
options: a:Yes — horns are for any communication purpose,b:No — horns should only be used to warn other drivers of a hazard or to avoid a collision,c:Yes, as long as it is not between 10 PM and 7 AM,d:Only when another driver is at fault
note: Nevada's vehicle code specifies that horns are for safety use only — to warn of a hazard or to prevent a collision. Using your horn for non-safety reasons (expressing frustration, greeting friends) is prohibited, though enforcement is rare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the primary danger of driving in heavy Las Vegas traffic after a light rain?
options: a:Sand washed onto the road from the desert reduces traction,b:Light rain mixes with oil on the road surface, making it extremely slippery,c:Sudden flooding always occurs after any rain in Las Vegas,d:Visibility improves dramatically after rain
note: After a dry period, rain mixes with accumulated oil and grease on Nevada road surfaces, creating a very slippery film. This 'first rain' hazard is especially dangerous in urban areas like Las Vegas where vehicles deposit oil over time. Reduce speed and increase following distance during and after light rain.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: For how far may drivers travel in a center turn lane before making a left turn?
options: a:About 100–200 feet, or only as far as needed to safely prepare for the turn.,b:Up to 500 feet.,c:There is no distance limit; it may be used as a travel lane.
note: A center left‑turn lane is for preparing and making left turns, not for through travel. In many states, you may not drive more than about 200 feet in this lane before beginning your turn, and you should enter it only close enough to the turn to safely slow and complete the maneuver.

section-name: Vehicle Ownership & Responsibilities
question: A curb painted which color indicates a loading zone or other parking restriction?
options: a:Yellow,b:Blue,c:White
note: A yellow curb usually marks a loading zone or other limited-time parking area. You may be allowed to stop only long enough to load or unload passengers or freight, and local signs or rules will specify the exact restrictions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a yield sign, you must:
options: a:Slow down and yield to pedestrians and traffic, stopping if necessary,b:Always come to a complete stop even if the way is clear,c:Have automatic right-of-way
note: At a yield sign, you must slow down and be ready to stop. You must yield to pedestrians and to any traffic that has the right-of-way, and only proceed when it is safe. A complete stop is required if other road users would be affected.

section-name: Vehicle Ownership & Responsibilities
question: What are the driving risks associated with worn or bald tires?
options: a:Can make turning and handling more difficult.,b:Are more likely to hydroplane on wet roads.,c:Can increase your stopping distance.,d:All of the above.
note: Worn or bald tires greatly reduce traction. This increases your stopping distance, makes it harder to turn or handle the vehicle, and raises the risk of hydroplaning on wet roads. Keeping tires in good condition is essential for safe braking and steering control.

section-name: Vehicle Ownership & Responsibilities
question: When should you use your parking brake?
options: a:Every time you park.,b:Only when parking on an incline.,c:Only when parked in a driveway.
note: You should set the parking brake every time you park, whether on a hill or on level ground. Using the parking brake helps keep the vehicle from rolling and reduces strain on the transmission, providing an extra layer of safety.

section-name: Special Situations & Road Users
question: Is it unlawful to share a lane with a motorcycle?
options: a:True,b:False
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, and other drivers should not crowd or share that lane side‑by‑side with them. A motorcycle needs space to maneuver and to avoid road hazards, and a car in the same lane can easily sideswipe or force the rider off the road.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: What causes 'highway hypnosis'?
options: a:Frequent rest stops.,b:Too much sleep the night before a trip.,c:Staring at the roadway for long periods without active scanning.,d:Listening to loud music.
note: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead for long periods without actively scanning mirrors, instruments, and the road environment. Your mind drifts, you become less alert, and your reaction time slows, even though your eyes are technically open.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Stop immediately.,b:Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.,c:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue through the intersection.
note: A solid yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely; if you are too close to stop safely, continue through with caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Coming to a complete stop, yielding to cross traffic and pedestrians, then proceeding when clear describes the meaning of which signal?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, you must yield to any cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers respond to a steady yellow arrow signal?
options: a:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,b:Should slow to a stop, if it is safe to do so.,c:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected signal is ending; stop if you can do so safely unless already in the intersection.

section-name: Safe & Defensive Driving Practices
question: If your vehicle's accelerator sticks open, what is the safest procedure?
options: a:Blow your horn.,b:Slam on your brakes.,c:Shift to neutral, brake smoothly, steer to a safe area, then turn off the ignition once stopped.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep control of the vehicle first. Shift to neutral, apply the brakes smoothly, and steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place. Once you are safely off the road and stopped, then turn off the ignition. Turning the key too early can lock the steering or disable power steering and brakes, making it harder to control the car.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is part of correct passing procedure?
options: a:Use your mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot when passing to the left.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes to pass and ensure there is no oncoming traffic.,c:When passing, wait until you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror before returning to your original lane.,d:All of the above
note: Safe passing requires signaling in advance, checking mirrors and blind spots, and making sure there is enough clear space ahead. After passing, do not move back into the lane until you can see the front of the passed vehicle (both headlights at night) in your rearview mirror.

section-name: Special Situations & Road Users
question: Why must you use extra caution near a pedestrian using a white cane?
options: a:They may be deaf.,b:They are likely a police officer.,c:They are visually impaired and may not see your vehicle.,d:They will always yield to cars.
note: A white cane (with or without a red tip) or a guide dog identifies a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. They may not see your vehicle or be able to judge its speed, so you must slow down, yield the right‑of‑way, and be prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians.,b:Stop and look for nearby police cars.,c:Maintain your normal driving speed.
note: A green light allows you to proceed, but it does not give you the right to endanger others. When turning right on green, you must yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any traffic already in the intersection before completing your turn.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: Which statement about a work zone is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be moving or stationary and are marked with orange signs; drivers should slow down and pay extra attention.,b:Work zones are always stationary and use black and white signs.,c:Work zones do not require drivers to change behavior.,d:Work zones require you to stop at all times.
note: Work zones can be stationary (like a fixed construction site) or moving (such as a line‑painting or pothole‑repair crew). They are typically marked with orange warning signs, cones, and other devices. Drivers must slow down, obey posted work‑zone speed limits, and pay close attention to workers, equipment, and changing traffic patterns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a fire engine is following you but not using its emergency signals, how should you respond?
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If a fire engine or other emergency vehicle is behind you but is not using its lights or siren, it is operating as a regular vehicle. You are not required to pull over or clear the lane; instead, continue driving normally, obeying all traffic laws and maintaining safe following distance and speed.

section-name: Signs, Signals & Road Markings
question: When a curb is painted green, what does it normally indicate?
options: a:Drivers may park for a limited time.,b:No stopping at any time.,c:Handicapped parking only.,d:Loading and unloading only.
note: A green-painted curb typically means you may stop or park for a limited time, as indicated by nearby signs or markings. It is intended for short-term parking, so you must obey the posted time limits.

section-name: Special Situations & Road Users
question: What is required when you encounter an emergency vehicle using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:Speed up to pass it quickly.,b:Ignore it and keep driving.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and maintain your lane.,d:Yield the right-of-way and follow any instructions given over loudspeaker.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop if possible, allowing it to pass. Obey any instructions given over a loudspeaker and proceed only after the emergency vehicle has passed and it is safe.

section-name: Special Situations & Road Users
question: When a crossing guard directs traffic in a school zone, how must you respond?
options: a:Follow the crossing guard's directions.,b:Copy surrounding drivers and ignore the guard.,c:Assume the guard lacks authority and continue.,d:Accelerate through the zone to clear it quickly.
note: Crossing guards have legal authority to direct traffic in school zones. You must obey their instructions just as you would a traffic signal or police officer and drive with extra caution around children.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving well under the posted speed limit is generally:
options: a:Always safe,b:Recommended at all times,c:Potentially dangerous and can force others to take risks
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be hazardous because it causes other drivers to brake or change lanes unexpectedly and may encourage risky passing. You should drive at a speed that is safe for conditions while not unnecessarily obstructing traffic.

section-name: Alcohol, Drugs & Impaired Driving
question: Which of these will help reverse the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Hot coffee.,b:Time.,c:Fresh air.
note: Only time reduces your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize alcohol at its own slow rate; coffee, cold showers, or fresh air may make you feel more awake but do not make you less impaired or safer to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to use a shared center turn lane?
options: a:As a travel lane to pass other vehicles.,b:To make a left turn onto another street, road, or driveway.,c:To make a right turn onto another street or highway.
note: A shared center turn lane is reserved for vehicles making left turns from either direction. You may use it to turn left onto another street, road, or driveway, or to wait to turn left from a side street or driveway onto the main road. It must not be used as a through lane or for passing other vehicles.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Overcorrect with sharp steering.,b:Steer in the direction you want the vehicle to go and remain calm.,c:Turn into oncoming traffic.,d:Brake hard immediately.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go. This is often described as steering in the direction of the skid. Avoid hard braking and sudden steering inputs, which can make the skid worse.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a street from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must honk your horn so approaching vehicles and pedestrians know to give you room.,b:Must drive slowly to allow approaching vehicles and pedestrians time to get out of your way.,c:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must stop before the sidewalk or curb and yield to pedestrians and all traffic on the main road. Only proceed when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching closely enough to be a hazard.

section-name: Driving in Special Conditions
question: Road surfaces become especially slippery when?
options: a:During the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm,b:After it has been raining for several hours,c:The day after it rains
note: When rain first begins, oil and residue on the road surface mix with the water and rise to the top, making the pavement very slick for the first several minutes. As rain continues, much of this washes away and traction generally improves, though you must still drive carefully.
